Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 6) demonstrates a small, hypoplastic right lung with diffuse opacity and ipsilateral mediastinal shift (dextroposition of the heart), which are hallmark features of Scimitar syndrome (hypogenetic lung syndrome). While the classic "scimitar" vein is best seen on the CT scans (Figures 4 and 5), option B correctly identifies the associated parenchymal and mediastinal findings visible on the radiograph.
